observations: Photo 0: Front view of a silver Dell all-in-one desktop wrapped in plastic. The Dell logo is visible on the bottom bezel. The screen is covered in plastic, reflecting light and surroundings.
Photo 1: Side/rear view of the same unit, showing the Dell logo on the back panel and the stand. Ports are visible on the back, but not clearly readable. The unit is still wrapped in plastic.
Photo 2: Front view similar to photo 0, with the same plastic wrap and Dell logo on the bezel. The screen remains obscured.
All photos show the unit in a retail-like setting with other Dell devices on shelves in the background, also wrapped in plastic.
No visible model number or specification label is readable in any photo.
The seller claims it is a touchscreen, but no evidence of touch functionality is visible in the photos.

claims.evidence: The Dell brand is visible in photos 0, 1, and 2. The 'all-in-one' form factor is visible. However, no evidence confirms it is a touchscreen — no touch indicators, no demonstration, and no visible model that confirms touchscreen capability.
These are performance and condition claims. The unit is wrapped in plastic, so physical condition cannot be assessed. Functionality (fast, ready to use) cannot be verified remotely.
The Dell brand is confirmed. The Intel CoreTM claim cannot be verified — no visible CPU label or specification sticker is readable in any photo.

risks.proof: A close-up photo of the screen showing touch sensors or a demonstration video of touch functionality.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a non-touchscreen all-in-one, which is significantly cheaper.

risks.risk: Unit is not working or has hidden damage
risks.proof: A video showing the unit powered on, displaying the desktop, and responding to input.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, which reduces value substantially.

risks.risk: Model is outdated or low-spec (e.g., old generation Intel Core, low RAM, small SSD)
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model label or specification sticker on the back or base of the unit.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the lowest common model in the Dell all-in-one range, assuming worst-case specs.

risks.risk: Unit is refurbished or has been used, not 'clean' as claimed
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the screen, bezel, and stand without plastic wrap, showing any scratches, marks, or wear.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as used/refurbished, not new or clean.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the model label or specification sticker on the back or base of the unit.
A video showing the unit powered on and functioning, including screen display and keyboard/mouse input.
A close-up photo of the screen without plastic wrap to check for damage or touch functionality.
A photo of the ports and any included accessories (power cable, keyboard, mouse).
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Dell all-in-one desktop, but critical details such as model, touchscreen capability, and working condition are unverified. Without proof of these, the price cannot be determined accurately, and the item must be priced at its worst-case scenario, which requires further evidence.
